result.journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
result.keywords: Modern systems increasingly need both memory-safety enforcement and network visibility, yet practical deployments must balance overhead, coverage, and usability. This paper studies a unified family of hardware-assisted guards that combine address-range validation with compact flow accounting to support both application memory protection and packet-level telemetry. We analyze the design across hardware, operating system, compiler, and runtime layers, focusing on performance overhead, security guarantees, and reconfigurability. The proposed framework presents a generalized family structure with interchangeable policies for memory checks and traffic counters, enabling low-overhead deployment under varied accuracy goals. We also compare the approach with conventional software-only safety and measurement techniques, and outline directions for future architecture extensions that better support adaptive protection and scalable observation.
result.title: Adaptive Guard Families for Hardware-Assisted Memory and Traffic Measurement.
